title: A.R.M.O.R. description of one spoken turn, the metadata part of the binary voice request
description: The `meta` part of a `multipart/form-data` request to POST /api/v1/voice/turn (and to the voice gateway's /v1/turn): what the audio part is and what the sender wants back. The audio is raw binary, not base64. `language` is the language of the person; `encoding`, `sample_rate` and `channels` say what the audio is (today only 16 kHz 16-bit signed little-endian mono PCM); `reply_audio` says how the spoken answer comes back: `base64` (the default, as in the older raw request: an `audio` field inside the JSON answer), `binary` (a second multipart part, 33 percent smaller and needing no decoding in the panel) or `none` (text only). The part is optional: without it the language is the one of the X-Armor-Language header (English when there is none) and the answer is as in the older request.
